title: Extended response: group behaviour and bias
stem: Section C concept-based extended response. In the real paper this is one 15-mark essay; here it is split into a knowledge part and an evaluation part.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Outline one theory that explains conflict between groups.
markscheme: theory identified, e.g. social identity theory (Tajfel & Turner, 1979) or realistic conflict theory (Sherif)
key processes described, e.g. categorization, identification, comparison / competition for limited resources
how this leads to in-group favouritism or hostility
supporting study outlined, e.g. Tajfel et al. (1971) minimal groups / Sherif et al. Robbers Cave
clear link from the study to the theory

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: To what extent does bias in research limit our understanding of group behaviour?
markscheme: the concept of bias is clearly defined (e.g. sampling, cultural, researcher bias, demand characteristics)
sampling bias: e.g. Robbers Cave used a small group of similar boys; Tajfel used Bristol schoolboys
cultural bias: e.g. findings from Western samples may not generalize; Bond & Smith (1996) show conformity varies with culture
demand characteristics: e.g. in minimal group studies participants may have guessed they were expected to favour their group
researcher bias / ethics: Sherif's team engineered conflict and interpreted observations
counterpoint: replications across samples and methods (e.g. many minimal group replications) reduce the impact of bias
counterpoint: field settings increase ecological validity even if control is lower
balanced judgement answering "to what extent" with justification
well-organized response using research as evidence throughout
parts.notes: Top answers use bias as the organising concept rather than listing study details.
